answer: An AI-agent market admits N voting identities per round only after its contract burns N native tokens per identity. With H other voters, a farm of n aliases pays n(n+H) tokens; adding one costs 2n+H+1 extra. Admission is batched, so the final N sets everyone's charge. Splitting funds among raven, glacier and quill wallets cannot reuse burned tokens or reduce N. Every identity pays again each round, so resetting keys or pre-aging aliases earns no discount.
